- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next period; reduce forecast peak by 10–15% to account for momentum decay.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of gradual upward correction.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and model forecasts are flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or recent price action is erratic.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “low-high-low” cycles, model tends to misread trend direction; favor smoother, less volatile path unless sentiment confirms strong breakout.
